general: All 65 families have an exhaustive independent reference (20213 released typed questions, 0 unsupported, 0 sampled). 15388 multiple-choice presentations checked (exactly one option equals the derived answer and is the keyed one): 0 bad. 15576 word forms: answer equals typed answer for all; word WORDING read for roughly one to three templates per family (about 40 families), not exhaustively; option order of native-choice word forms (:w) was not exported and not checked.
nativeChoiceOptions: For the 16 families whose typed form is itself multiple choice (apcartl, apintch, aqbinmod, aqbinp, aqonto, aqrel, adestchk, aematch, akcode, akdirinv, akdsort, anpow0, anpts, atclass, atconv, atstmt) export.ts exports only the key letter. The option texts were exported separately with a read-only script that calls problemOf(id).options (data only, no solving code was read) into /tmp/certout/sets-reasoning/choice_options.json; the derived answer is matched to the one option whose wording states it and the letter compared with the key.
adestchk: "Sensible" is undefined in the statement. Reference: estimate = rounded sum/difference (half-up to tens); sensible if |given - estimate| <= 10 (the largest possible rounding error), too big/small if >= 30 away, otherwise Ambiguous. In the released data there is a clean gap (|d|<=10 or |d|>=41), so no question is borderline.
roundingTies: adest (80 questions), adestcost (65) and adestchk (58) contain numbers ending in 5; reference rounds half up (school convention); stored answers agree. A half-down reading would change those answers.
afdigits: 45 questions use a digit 0; numbers with a leading 0 are not counted as 2-/3-digit numbers (reference and stored agree).
atstmt: Which-is-a-statement items classified by me: declarative with a definite truth value (true or false) = statement, including false ones such as "9 + 5 = 15."; open sentences (x + 3 = 5, y is greater than 3), questions, commands and exclamations are not statements.
anpts: Reference flags Ambiguous when a triangle is both right-angled and isosceles (two listed options true); this never occurs in the released data.
akcrypt/akcrypt2: Brute force over all digit assignments; akcrypt run both with and without the leading-digit-nonzero convention (not stated for akcrypt) and the asked letter is the same in every question.
aqonto: N read both as {1,2,..} and {0,1,..}: same class in every question. Injectivity on R by collision search plus monotonicity test of f on a grid, surjectivity by sympy function_range; Z/N by enumeration in a window: appropriate for the linear/quadratic/cubic/abs shapes present, not a general proof.
aqbinp: Polynomial operations: exact symbolic identity test; max/min/|.| operations: exhaustive rational-grid search (25^2 pairs, 25^2*13 triples) for a counterexample, which also settles the associative cases by the closed forms a|b| and max{a,c}.
afhidden/afriver/afnim: Triangle counts by exact-coordinate enumeration of line triples; river crossings by BFS over states; take-away games by memoised minimax (normal and misere): all independent of the closed-form patterns.
refBugsFixed: A first run of aqbinp reported 1 mismatch (a*b = a|b|): reference parsing bug (aAbs(b)); after the fix the stored answer (associative, not commutative) is confirmed by hand: (a|b|)|c| = a|b||c| = a|b|c||.
